reflection.lesson: Engineering estimates establish a feasible 68.33 km baseline at 17 m/s. Cruise has 105.42 Wh after reserve/overhead; hardware plus profile drag contributes 2.30 of 3.59 N. Static margin is 8.99% within the 5–20% band. Structure passes, but wing deflection is 44.2 mm against a 52.5 mm limit, constraining weight cuts.
reflection.next_focus: Prioritize parasite-drag reduction, especially hardware/profile drag, before structural thinning. Keep 150 Wh and the 0.5 kg mission payload fixed; recheck static margin, stress and deflection. Protect max speed ≥18.05 m/s and payload capacity ≥0.912 kg (95% of baseline). Compare nominal and adverse range against 68.33 and 51.84 km.

tool.explanation:
This is a constant-cruise energy sensitivity calculator, not a flight simulator. Supply all five inputs; invalid inputs raise ValueError. Reserve is deducted first, then non-cruise overhead. Your history does not explicitly specify reserve_fraction or overhead_wh, so these must be supplied rather than assuming all 150 Wh is available for cruise.

Compare drag improvements by changing cruise_power_w at a matched speed, using an external propulsion-efficiency estimate to translate drag into electrical power. A 10% cruise-power reduction increases range by 11.11% when speed and cruise energy remain unchanged.

Compare hover-energy improvements by changing overhead_wh. For constant hover power, hover energy is hover_power_w * hover_seconds / 3600; include transition and other non-cruise energy as appropriate. Each Wh saved adds 1 / wh_per_km kilometers without changing cruise Wh/km. At iteration 2's cruise point (67.4106 W, 14 m/s), consumption is approximately 1.33751 Wh/km, so saving 1 Wh of overhead adds about 0.748 km.

Your iterations use different cruise speeds, so their changes do not isolate drag reduction alone. This utility does not evaluate geometry, stability, structural limits, or flight feasibility.
